dedupe_keys.name: the green grid free cooling maps and tools air side and water side economiser hours

description: The Green Grid, an industry consortium on data-centre efficiency, published maps and online tools showing how many hours a year a data centre in a given place can be cooled with outside air or water instead of mechanical chillers, known as free cooling or economisation. The first maps, from 2009, used ASHRAE's 2008 recommended ranges of temperature and humidity; white paper 46, from 2012, updated them for the wider allowable classes ASHRAE introduced in 2011. It found that under class A2, allowing up to 35 degrees Celsius for short periods, 75 per cent of North America, 97 per cent of Europe and 14 per cent of Japan could use air-side economisers in every hour of a typical year, and that under class A3, up to 40 degrees, 91 to 99 per cent of locations could. The maps rest on hourly weather bin data: about ten years (1999 to 2009) for North America by postcode and five to ten years for European and Japanese airport stations, and the companion tools let users set their IT load and temperature and humidity limits to compute economiser hours for a location. Coverage: North America, Europe and Japan. Format and access: PDF white papers with maps, free; the online calculators were on The Green Grid website. Caveats: based on historical climate, so hours will fall as heat and humidity rise; maps are coarse. Simulation uses: cooling energy and resilience of data centres under climate scenarios, siting studies and heatwave stress tests. Related records: the London heatwave data-centre case shows the failure mode when outdoor air is too hot.
